```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", eval = TRUE)
```

Which grouping/filtering approach is *right* for a given instrument, acquisition
mode, or compound class is an open research question, not something carpeDIAMS
tries to settle once and for all. The `grouper`, `group_statistics_fn`, and
`filter_fn` arguments to [`process_pseudo_spec()`]/[`clean_pseudo_spectra()`]
exist so you can swap in your own answer without forking the package. This
vignette walks through evaluating one, using a real, shipped example rather
than a synthetic one.

## The fixture

`inst/testdata/FT00964/` is a real slice of a production carpeDIAMS run — not
synthetic data. It's feature `FT00964` (precursor m/z ≈ 166.05), across the 10
samples that carry it, trimmed to exactly the rows the real query in
`batch_get_feature_data()` ever touches for this feature (pool/pointers
parquets, same on-disk contract as any other carpeDIAMS run — see
`vignette("dag-cli")` for what that contract looks like at scale). It's small
(~600 KB) specifically so it can ship with the package and run in this
vignette.

```{r load-fixture}
library(carpeDIAMS)
library(data.table)

fixture_dir <- system.file("testdata", "FT00964", package = "carpeDIAMS")
fd <- readRDS(file.path(fixture_dir, "fd.rds"))
fd[, c("mzmed", "rtmed")]
```

Pull the raw MS1+MS2 rows the same way `clean_pseudo_spectra()` does
internally — connect, then fetch:

```{r fetch-raw}
con <- setup_connection(fixture_dir)
raw <- batch_get_feature_data("FT00964", con)
DBI::dbDisconnect(con, shutdown = TRUE)

nrow(raw)
length(unique(raw$sample))
```

`raw` has one row per (sample, MS1 scan, matched MS2 fragment) — exactly
what [`process_pseudo_spec()`] expects as `dt`.

## Comparing groupers

Try the default (`ppm_upgma`) against `iaac_grouper` at the production
tolerance:

```{r compare-default}
mz_target <- fd["FT00964", "mzmed"]

stats_ppm  <- process_pseudo_spec(raw, mz_target = mz_target,
                                  grouper = ppm_upgma(ppm = 30))
stats_iaac <- process_pseudo_spec(raw, mz_target = mz_target,
                                  grouper = iaac_grouper(k = 2, p0 = 12, Isat = 1e4))

# top fragment by correlation, under each grouper
stats_ppm[order(-abs(correlation))][1, .(fragment_mz, count, correlation)]
stats_iaac[order(-abs(correlation))][1, .(fragment_mz, count, correlation)]
```

Both agree closely here. That's not always true, and this fixture is a good
place to see exactly why.

## A concrete `p0` sensitivity example

`process_pseudo_spec()` clusters **within each sample first**, then clusters
the resulting per-sample evidence-weighted points **across samples** — see
`?grouper-contract` for the full rationale. That second (cross-sample) pass
has to be wide enough to absorb real between-sample calibration drift, not
just within-sample scan noise. `p0` (for `iaac_grouper`/`pelt_grouper`) sets
that width. Too tight, and a single real fragment gets reported as two:

```{r p0-sensitivity}
for (p0 in c(4, 8, 12)) {
  g <- iaac_grouper(k = 1, p0 = p0, Isat = 1e5)
  s <- process_pseudo_spec(raw, mz_target = mz_target, grouper = g)
  near67 <- s[fragment_mz > 67.04 & fragment_mz < 67.06]
  cat(sprintf("p0=%2d: %d group(s) near 67.05 Da (counts: %s)\n",
              p0, nrow(near67), paste(near67$count, collapse = ", ")))
}
```

At `p0 = 4`, the fragment near 67.054 Da is reported as two separate groups
~10 ppm apart — real between-sample calibration drift for this feature, wider
than a `p0` sized for within-run precision alone. By `p0 = 12` they merge into
one well-supported group. This is exactly the kind of thing to check when
tuning a grouper for a new instrument or acquisition mode: pick a handful of
real, multi-sample features and look for this pattern before trusting a `p0`
value across a whole cohort.

## Writing your own grouper

A grouper is a factory function returning a closure with a fixed signature —
see `?grouper-contract`. [`process_pseudo_spec()`] calls the *same* grouper
instance for both passes (once per-sample, once across-sample); what differs
between the two calls is which arguments are populated, not which function is
used.

```{r custom-grouper}
# A trivial custom grouper: fixed ppm tolerance, but reject a merge if the
# combined evidence is too thin (n < 3) - contrived, just to show the shape.
sparse_aware_grouper <- function(ppm = 20, min_n = 3L) {
  force(ppm); force(min_n)
  function(mz, intensity = NULL, target_mz = NULL, scan = NULL, ms1_int = NULL) {
    if (length(mz) < min_n) return(seq_along(mz))  # too little evidence: don't merge anything
    fast_1D_upgma_grouping_cpp(mz, maxDiff = 1e-6 * target_mz * ppm)
  }
}

validate_grouper(sparse_aware_grouper())

stats_custom <- process_pseudo_spec(raw, mz_target = mz_target,
                                    grouper = sparse_aware_grouper(ppm = 20))
nrow(stats_custom)
```

[`validate_grouper()`] sanity-checks the contract (right output length, no
more groups than distinct input values) against small synthetic input before
you run it against real data — do this once when wiring up something new.

## Writing your own filter

Statistics (`group_statistics_fn`) and filtering (`filter_fn`) are separate
closures for the same reason grouping is swappable — see `?stats-contract`
and `?filter-contract`. The default pair is [`correlation_statistics()`] +
[`correlation_filtering()`]; [`apex_correlation_statistics()`] +
[`apex_correlation_filtering()`] add intra-sample MS1↔MS2 apex-agreement
columns and thresholds, for when correlation alone lets through fragments
from a coeluting compound.

```{r custom-filter}
# A stricter filter: require both a higher correlation AND more supporting
# (sample, ms1_scan) cells than the package default.
strict_filter <- function(stats) {
  stats[correlation > 0.8 & count >= 30]
}

clean_pseudo_spectra(
  targets        = "FT00964",
  file_directory = fixture_dir,
  fd             = fd,
  grouper        = iaac_grouper(k = 2, p0 = 12, Isat = 1e4),
  filter_fn      = strict_filter,
  report         = FALSE,
  mgf_dir        = NULL,
  progress       = FALSE
)[, .(feature_id, mz_g2, count, r, fdr)]
```

## Where this is checked automatically

`tests/testthat/test-process_pseudo_spec.R` pins the numbers shown above (the
`p0 = 12` top-group correlation, the `p0 = 4` vs `p0 = 12` split/merge
behavior) as regression tests against this same fixture. If you change the
grouping design and those tests start failing, that's either a real
regression or a deliberate change worth calling out explicitly — not
something to silently update without checking why the numbers moved.
